groups.title: Modern JavaScript Core
groups.question: You are writing the data-loading code for a SvelteKit page that imports helpers from other files and fetches from an API. Explain the modern JavaScript you rely on.

followUps.Arrow functions and destructuring syntax: How do arrow functions and destructuring reduce boilerplate?
followUps.ES modules import and export system: What is the difference between named and default exports?
followUps.Promises and async/await control flow: How do you handle errors in async code so they do not fail silently?

evidence.text: Arrow functions give a short syntax for functions, often used for callbacks.
Destructuring pulls fields out of objects and arrays into variables.
Both appear constantly in component and load function code.
A module can have many named exports, imported by their exact names.
A module has at most one default export, imported under any name.
Mixing them up causes undefined imports or build errors.
A promise represents a value or error that arrives later.
await pauses the function until the promise settles.
try and catch handle failures; unhandled rejections hide errors or crash.

groups.title: TypeScript Type System
groups.question: SvelteKit generates types for your routes, and you are writing typed load functions. Explain the TypeScript you need.

followUps.Interfaces and type aliases in TypeScrip: When would you use an interface and when a type alias?
followUps.Generics and utility types overview: How do generics appear in SvelteKit's typed helpers?

evidence.text: Both describe the shape of objects and function signatures.
Interfaces can be extended and merged.
Type aliases can also name unions and other complex types.
Generics let one type or function work with many types safely.
SvelteKit's generated types like PageLoad use generics to describe each route's data.
Utility types like Partial and Pick derive new types from existing ones.

groups.title: Vite Dev Server
groups.question: You are adding a plugin to your SvelteKit project and notice component state resets when you edit some files. Explain how Vite powers development.

followUps.Vite project structure and config file: What does vite.config.ts control in a SvelteKit project?
followUps.Hot Module Replacement during developmen: How does hot module replacement work, and why might state reset?

evidence.text: Vite is the build tool SvelteKit runs on.
vite.config.ts adds plugins and customises the dev server and build.
The SvelteKit plugin is registered there.

notEnough: Only saying Vite builds the project.

evidence.text: HMR updates only the changed module in the browser.
This avoids a full page reload during development.
Some changes cannot be patched in place, so the module reloads and its state is lost.

notEnough: Only saying HMR updates the page.

groups.title: DOM and Browser APIs
groups.question: You need to measure an element after it appears and debug a failing API request in a SvelteKit app. Explain when you use browser APIs directly.

followUps.DOM querying and event listener basics: Why must DOM code run inside onMount?
followUps.Fetch API for HTTP requests: Why is it useful to know the raw Fetch API when SvelteKit wraps it?

evidence.text: Svelte usually handles the DOM for you.
Components also render on the server, where the DOM does not exist.
onMount runs only in the browser after the component is added, so DOM APIs are safe there.

notEnough: Only saying onMount runs on mount.

evidence.text: SvelteKit's data loading is built on fetch.
fetch resolves even for error statuses, so response.ok must be checked.
Knowing the raw API helps debug network issues and responses.
